title: One slider, three ways: what modular editing saves
question: hazelgrove/hazel#2597 has no modular editing, and #2635 has it, from #2469 (modular editors). How long does one slider change take on a complex picture, the Livelit Playground's Full Body slide? The hypothesis: #2635 is much faster, especially in its UX outline mode, showing only the slider and the picture, because it doesn't reprocess the unrelated code. A third set-up separates the two halves of that hypothesis.

builds.name: A
builds.note: no modular editing; has ^report(7)'s fix (c07bdacead), so its worker's stream messages are throttled as on #2635; the whole program on screen, with its livelits; dev build, served locally

builds.name: C
builds.note: modular editing; the whole program on screen, with its livelits (the outline's dev mode); dev build, served locally

builds.name: B
builds.note: modular editing; only two cells on screen, the slider and the picture (the outline's UX mode, every GUI row's chip switched off except 'arm_length' and 'drawn')

builds.name: B, fixed; C, fixed
builds.note: the reuse check compares lexemes in the same memoized walk as structure; on #2635 as cbdab791f5

builds.name: C, with the index's fix
builds.note: the page's index of the elaboration stops at expressions; on #2635 as 8717564a5f

builds.name: reuse-diag
builds.note: a temporary build on local branch perf/2635-reuse-diag, not pushed, that counted IncrEval.reuse_check's outcomes and printed them per request; its own sampling slowed it, so no time in the report comes from it

runtime: headless Firefox over WebDriver (the report states no version), a fresh profile per set-up, dev builds served locally; one set-up at a time, on one laptop. The Full Body slide's text is identical on both branches.
runs: Twelve changes per set-up, after two warm-up changes, each a real pointer drag of the 'arm length' slider to a length not drawn before, the same twelve lengths in each set-up. Profiles: three changes per set-up, and six more each for B with the reuse check's fix and for C with the index's fix. Reuse counts: per slider change, steady state, from the reuse-diag build, its worker console copied to a file by Firefox (devtools.console.stdout.content).

measures.release to redraw: s: from the slider's pointerup to the first moment a large picture's markup differed from before the drag, checked every 200 ms in the page (so it works whether a picture is patched or rebuilt)
measures.Against C: ratio: a set-up's median over C's
measures.Per change, profiled: ms per change, from the Gecko profiler sampling every 1 ms, the page's main thread and the eval worker together; windows from each pointerup to its redraw, from marks the page set (13.3, 1.8, 4.2 and 2.2 s for A, C, B and B fixed). Rows overlap: a function's time includes what it calls. Profiled times run longer than the clock
measures.printing code (of_segment): ms, profiled: the code view in A and C, the autosave's text in B
measures.segment_to_string: ms, profiled: the program turned into text
measures.live_html: ms, profiled: livelit views without their memo
measures.memo_view: ms, profiled: livelit views through their memo
measures.Worker: the reuse check: ms, profiled: reuse_check on the eval worker
measures.Worker: evaluating: ms, profiled: run_scheduled_slice on the eval worker, which includes most of the reuse check
measures.Checks: count per change: the reuse check's calls
measures.the hash matches: count per change: parts whose hash matched a cached entry (one lookup)
measures.the slow path: count per change: parts whose hash differs but which are equal; the hash covers ids as well as structure
measures.time on the slow path: ms per change: the slow path's time, structure (memoized) plus lexemes
measures.the index: ms, profiled: the page's index of the elaboration (where each expression starts and ends), built once per change: 204 of C's 949 ms page update before 8717564a5f, 115 ms after (six changes)

times: the in-page check every 200 ms bounds the clock's resolution; profiled times run long, so the profile's rows say where the time goes and the clock says how much

figures.1.2 s: C: #2635, the whole program on screen (median of 12)
figures.3.5 s: B: #2635, only the slider and the picture (median of 12)
figures.1.26 s: B with the reuse check fixed (median of 12)

readings.B with the fix, range: 1.06-1.9 s, with one change at 3.8 s (median 1.26 s of 12)
readings.C with the index's fix, median: 1.37 s of 12, against 1.23 s before, 'inside the noise of a check that runs every 200 ms'
readings.B, only the slider's cell open (reuse co: slow-path checks fall from 122 to 4 per change

cited.number: 3.5 s of statics against 16 ms per item
cited.what: a Kids' Choice release on #2597 and #2635
the subterm each enclosing let traced in the slow path's lexeme comparison, which is quadratic
tests passing with cbdab791f5: the Evaluator, Evaluator.Incremental, IncrSlides, CallMemo and Equality groups

updates: Corrected on 2026-10-13: #2597's terms carry no lexemes (they came to dev with 500c466b44, which #2597 lacks), so there is nothing to bring to #2597; dev compares lexemes by trace on every check (since 7de3875cd8), so the fix would suit it, with the hash shortcut. No new measurements.
provenance: No raw file was kept with this report: the WebDriver driver's output, the Gecko profiles and the reuse-diag build's console file were not saved with it. Every number here exists only as printed in the report.

update_2026_10_14.question: Are B and C similar once the same fixes are applied to each?

builds.name: C, B (with the print fixed)
builds.note: the autosave's print of a program with probes made linear (Triggers.refractor_seg_to_seg_with); sessions r84_*3-5 had the fix's first half (array slicing and one-ended ranges), r84_*6-7 both halves (also skipping segments with no probe pieces)
